features.description: Parent/child metadata + depth/cycle/repeated-finding guards. plan.md frontmatter gains an optional `orchestration` block with required-when-present fields. **Structured spawn identity (D001)**: instead of a free-form `spawn_finding_id`, the spawn metadata carries five fields — `parent_audit_id` (string, must match the `audit_id` of an envelope under the parent plan's audit/), `finding_id` (string, references the auditor-assigned finding identifier within that envelope's findings list — typically `audit_id#finding-N`), `finding_code` (string, the auditor's structured code — e.g. `EC5`, `S101`), `finding_class` (string, the category — `correctness`, `security`, `test_coverage`, etc.), AND `finding_signature` (deterministic SHA-256 hex prefix of `{finding_code}|{finding_class}|{normalized_issue}` where `normalized_issue` is whitespace-collapsed lowercase issue text). For `spawn_reason: operator_manual` plans, the five spawn fields are NOT required — the child_charter (F002) carries strategic_objective + return_condition instead. Top-level required orchestration fields: `parent_plan_id` (string, must reference an existing plan dir), `spawn_reason` (`auditor_finding | operator_manual`), `depth_limit` (int, defaults 3 — frontmatter MAY declare a LOWER value but cannot raise the platform cap, per D002). plan_loader validates the chain at dispatch time: walks parent_plan_id transitively to compute nesting depth; refuses dispatch if depth > depth_limit unless `--allow-depth N` CLI override is passed (D002 — CLI-only, never frontmatter upward); refuses if same plan_id appears twice in the chain (cycle); refuses if any parent plan in the chain has the same `finding_signature` recorded (repeated-finding hard stop — uses the signature hash, not just `(code, class)`, because `(EC5, correctness)` is too broad to gate on alone, per D001). Spawn authority enforced: only `auditor_finding` (with all five spawn fields and finding_id pointing into a parent audit envelope's findings list) OR `operator_manual` (no spawn fields required, but operator must declare strategic_objective + return_condition in the child_charter — F002 enforces). Implementer self-spawn rejected. Frontmatter is parsed by a new `nested_orchestration` module returning a structured `Orchestration` Pydantic model. Top-level plans (no parent) have `orchestration=None` and pass validation trivially. The `orchestration` block is plan.md frontmatter only — `audit.schema.json` and `features.schema.json` are unmodified. Anti-recursion thesis enforcement: depth cap + cycle detection + signature-based repeated-finding hard stop together make it impossible to spawn an unbounded chain of child plans 'fixing the same thing.'
steps: Add `scripts/jarvis_orchestrate/nested_orchestration.py` module: `SpawnFinding` Pydantic model (parent_audit_id, finding_id, finding_code, finding_class, finding_signature) + `Orchestration` Pydantic model (parent_plan_id, spawn_reason, spawn_finding: SpawnFinding | None, depth_limit). Helper `compute_finding_signature(finding_code, finding_class, issue) -> str` (deterministic SHA-256 hex prefix of `{code}|{class}|{normalized_issue}` where normalized_issue collapses whitespace + lowercases). Helpers `walk_parent_chain(plan_dir) -> list[plan_id]` (transitive walk), `compute_depth(plan_dir) -> int`, `check_depth(plan_dir, override_max: int | None = None)` (raises NestedOrchestrationError on violation; respects the LOWER of frontmatter depth_limit + override), `check_cycle(plan_dir)` (raises on plan_id appearing twice in chain), `check_repeated_finding(plan_dir)` (raises when current plan's finding_signature matches any parent's recorded signature).

Pydantic validators on Orchestration: `spawn_reason='auditor_finding'` requires non-None `spawn_finding`; `spawn_reason='operator_manual'` requires `spawn_finding=None`; `depth_limit <= 3` (frontmatter cannot exceed platform default — D002). On parse, recompute `finding_signature` from `(code, class, issue)` (looked up via parent_audit_id + finding_id) and compare to the declared signature; reject mismatches as drift evidence (auditor changed the finding text but the spawning child still references the old hash).

Extend `plan_loader.py`: parse the optional `orchestration` block from plan.md frontmatter into the Pydantic model; add a `LoadedPlan.orchestration: Orchestration | None` field; load is unchanged for top-level plans.

Wire validation into `supervisor.py`: at the top of both `dispatch_single_agent` and `dispatch_volley`, after plan_loader.load, if loaded.orchestration is not None, call check_depth + check_cycle + check_repeated_finding. Each raises NestedOrchestrationError on violation; the CLI surfaces the error with a non-zero exit (mirrors the cli.main catch path established in plan 005 F002 test).

Add CLI flag `--allow-depth N` to `python -m jarvis_orchestrate <plan_id> --volley` and `--single` paths. The flag is the ONLY way to dispatch above the effective depth_limit (D002 — frontmatter is bounded by the platform cap of 3; only operators at dispatch time can lift it). The override is recorded in the audit envelope's validation_performed list as a string `depth_override applied (N)` for audit-trail visibility.

Tests: `scripts/jarvis_orchestrate/tests/test_nested_orchestration.py` covers (a) Orchestration model parses valid frontmatter, rejects malformed (Pydantic ValidationError) — including spawn_reason/spawn_finding cross-field invariants; (b) compute_finding_signature is deterministic across whitespace + case variations of the same issue text; (c) walk_parent_chain returns [child, parent, grandparent, ...] for a 3-deep tree, [child] for a 2-deep, [] for a top-level; (d) check_depth raises at depth=4 with default limit=3, passes at depth=3, passes at depth=4 when --allow-depth=5 override; (e) frontmatter `depth_limit: 5` is CLAMPED to 3 (D002 — frontmatter cannot raise); (f) check_cycle raises when plan_id appears twice in the chain (synthetic broken plan dir); (g) check_repeated_finding raises when current plan's finding_signature matches a parent's signature even if `audit_id#finding-N` strings differ; (h) check_repeated_finding does NOT raise for two distinct findings that share `(code, class)` but differ in normalized_issue (signature differs); (i) supervisor.dispatch_volley refuses dispatch on each violation with non-zero exit; (j) `--allow-depth N` override path passes validation that would otherwise fail.
features.acceptance: (1) `scripts/jarvis_orchestrate/nested_orchestration.py` exists with `SpawnFinding` + `Orchestration` Pydantic models + helpers (`compute_finding_signature`, `walk_parent_chain`, `compute_depth`, `check_depth`, `check_cycle`, `check_repeated_finding`) + `NestedOrchestrationError` exception. (2) **Structured spawn identity (D001)**: SpawnFinding requires all five fields (parent_audit_id, finding_id, finding_code, finding_class, finding_signature). `compute_finding_signature` is deterministic across whitespace + case variations of issue text — verified by parametrized test with the same `(code, class, issue)` differing only in spaces/case yielding identical signatures. (3) `plan_loader.LoadedPlan` gains an optional `orchestration` field; top-level plans load identically to today (zero behavior change for plans without an `orchestration` frontmatter block). (4) `supervisor.dispatch_volley` and `dispatch_single_agent` both invoke the three guards (depth, cycle, repeated-finding) when orchestration is set; raise NestedOrchestrationError with audit_id + plan_id + finding_signature context (mirrors plan 005 F002 acceptance #5) BEFORE any agent dispatch or quota consumption. (5) **CLI-only depth override (D002)**: `--allow-depth N` on the `<plan-id> --volley` and `<plan-id>` (single-agent) paths is the ONLY mechanism for raising the cap; frontmatter `depth_limit` is clamped to a hard ceiling of 3 (parsed values > 3 are rejected at Pydantic-validation time, OR clamped silently — either way, frontmatter cannot raise the cap). The CLI override is recorded in `validation_performed` as `depth_override applied (N)` for audit-trail visibility. Verified by parametrized test that frontmatter `depth_limit: 5` raises ValidationError; `--allow-depth 5` succeeds. (6) **Spawn authority enforced**: `Orchestration.spawn_reason` is one of `auditor_finding | operator_manual` (Pydantic enum); when `spawn_reason=auditor_finding`, `spawn_finding` (the SpawnFinding model) is required; when `spawn_reason=operator_manual`, `spawn_finding=None` is required; mismatches raise ValidationError. (7) **Cycle detection**: parametrized test with synthetic plan dirs constructs a 3-plan cycle (A→B→C→A) and asserts `check_cycle` raises with both plan_ids in the message. (8) **Signature-based repeated-finding hard stop (D001)**: test with two parent plans whose findings share `(EC5, correctness)` but differ in normalized_issue → distinct signatures → child claiming a third EC5/correctness finding with a third distinct signature DOES NOT trigger the guard (signatures differ); a fourth child whose finding_signature matches one of the parents' DOES trigger NestedOrchestrationError citing the matching parent_plan_id + finding_signature. The signature-based rule prevents the broad `(code, class)`-only false-positive case. (9) **Default depth limit = 3**: verified by parametrized depth test (1, 2, 3 pass; 4 fails without override). (10) **Override path verified**: `--allow-depth 5` enables depth=4 dispatch; the audit envelope records the override. (11) plan.md without an `orchestration` block (i.e., every existing plan) loads and dispatches identically to today (zero regression). Verified by running `dispatch_volley` against a top-level plan in the synthetic test harness. (12) `audit.schema.json` and `features.schema.json` are unmodified — the change is in plan.md frontmatter parsing only. (13) NestedOrchestrationError messages contain enough context (parent plan_id, child plan_id, finding_signature, current depth, limit) for an operator to understand why dispatch was refused without reading source.

features.description: Child charter + commit policy (minimal, enforced at close-out). plan.md frontmatter gains an optional `child_charter` block valid only when `orchestration.parent_plan_id` is set. Required fields when present: `kind` (literal `'implementation'` for v1 — `'governance_design'` deferred to v2), `parent_objective` (text, ≤500 chars), `parent_acceptance_item` (text, the parent acceptance clause this child unblocks), `allowed_paths` (list of glob patterns; child writes restricted to these), `forbidden_decisions` (list, text pointers), `return_condition_summary` (one short text describing the observable signal — used to render the `## Return Condition` section template; the close-out memo's actual structured `status:` line is what enforcement reads), `may_edit_product_code` (bool, NO default — must be explicit per D003), `may_spawn_children` (bool, defaults false). Optional `commit_policy` block: `mode` (`child_commit | evidence_only`, **defaults to `evidence_only`** per D003 — code-writing authority must be explicit; `parent_squash` deferred to v2), `requires` (subset of `[patch_completeness, tests_pass, evidence_packaged]`). Cross-field invariant: when `commit_policy.mode='child_commit'`, `child_charter.may_edit_product_code` MUST be `true`; the inverse (mode='evidence_only' + may_edit_product_code=true) is also rejected as nonsensical. Enforcement is at close-out / evidence packaging time, NOT pre-impl gating. **`## Return Condition` section is a structured contract (D004), not substring matching.** signoff_writer parses `evidence/closeout-memo.md` for a markdown section literally headed `## Return Condition`; that section must contain a line matching `^status:\s*(satisfied|blocked|superseded)\s*$` (case-insensitive). Only `status: satisfied` permits the parent's F003 approve to clear `pre_resume_after_child`; `blocked` or `superseded` records the close-out but parent re-entry is refused with the recorded status surfaced. signoff_writer adds a `child_charter_compliance` check that runs when the plan has a `child_charter`: (a) compares `git diff` modified file paths against `allowed_paths` when `commit_policy.mode='child_commit'` (any file outside is a HARD blocker — signoff refuses to land); (b) asserts the `## Return Condition` section is present, well-formed, and `status:` is one of the three legal values; (c) asserts each `requires` item is documented as satisfied in the signoff envelope (e.g., `tests_pass: 469/475 + 6 skipped`). No runtime sandboxing of agent file access — the agent can technically write anywhere; the close-out check refuses to sign off if it did. Anti-recursion enforcement: `may_spawn_children` defaults false, so a v1 child plan cannot dispatch a grandchild without explicit operator approval (frontmatter override + a separate D-entry).
steps: Extend `nested_orchestration.py`: add `ChildCharter` Pydantic model (kind enum, parent_objective, parent_acceptance_item, allowed_paths, forbidden_decisions, return_condition_summary, may_edit_product_code, may_spawn_children) + `CommitPolicy` Pydantic model (mode enum default `evidence_only`, requires set). Validators: kind must be 'implementation' in v1 (governance_design rejected with deferral message); allowed_paths must be non-empty when present; return_condition_summary must be non-empty; may_edit_product_code has NO default (must be set explicitly per D003); commit_policy.mode default is `evidence_only`; cross-field invariant — `mode='child_commit'` requires `may_edit_product_code=true` AND vice versa: `mode='evidence_only'` requires `may_edit_product_code=false`.

Add `parse_return_condition_section(memo_path: Path) -> Literal['satisfied', 'blocked', 'superseded']` helper to nested_orchestration.py (D004). Reads `evidence/closeout-memo.md`, locates a markdown section whose heading is exactly `## Return Condition` (case-sensitive, leading whitespace permitted), within that section finds the FIRST line matching `^\s*status:\s*(satisfied|blocked|superseded)\s*$` (case-insensitive on the keyword and value), returns the lowercased status. Raises `ReturnConditionError` with specific reason on (a) section missing, (b) status line missing, (c) status value not in the allowed enum, (d) multiple status lines (ambiguous).

Extend `plan_loader.LoadedPlan`: add `child_charter` and `commit_policy` optional fields. Cross-validation: `child_charter` is rejected if `orchestration.parent_plan_id` is None (charter only valid on child plans). When charter is present and `commit_policy` is absent, fill commit_policy with default `mode=evidence_only, requires=[]`.

Modify `signoff_writer.py`: when LoadedPlan.child_charter is set, before writing signoff JSON, run `check_child_charter_compliance(loaded_plan, signoff_data)`. Three checks: (a) when `commit_policy.mode='child_commit'`: `git diff <last-merge-base>...HEAD --name-only` against allowed_paths globs (using fnmatch) — any file outside is a HARD blocker; (b) call `parse_return_condition_section(plan_dir / 'evidence' / 'closeout-memo.md')` — propagates ReturnConditionError as a ChildCharterViolation; the parsed status is recorded in signoff_data['return_condition_status']; (c) for each item in `commit_policy.requires`, assert the corresponding key appears in signoff_data (`tests_pass` → signoff_data must have a tests-summary field; `patch_completeness` → must reference a patch-completeness check; `evidence_packaged` → evidence_dir must be non-empty). Failures raise `ChildCharterViolation` with specific field + observed-vs-expected; signoff does NOT land.

CLI surface: when `python -m jarvis_orchestrate <plan_id>` runs to close-out and the plan has a child_charter, the close-out command prints the compliance summary (paths checked when applicable, return_condition status parsed, requires items satisfied) before writing signoff. Operator can re-run after fixing. The CLI also prints a stub `## Return Condition` template if the close-out memo is missing or the section is absent — operator pastes + fills + re-runs.

Tests: `test_child_charter.py` covers (a) ChildCharter model parses valid + rejects missing required fields (especially explicit may_edit_product_code); (b) cross-validation: charter without parent_plan_id is rejected; (c) cross-field invariant: `mode='child_commit' + may_edit_product_code=false` rejected; `mode='evidence_only' + may_edit_product_code=true` rejected; (d) parse_return_condition_section returns each of the three legal statuses for well-formed inputs; (e) parse_return_condition_section raises on missing section, missing status line, illegal status value (e.g., 'partial'), multiple status lines; (f) compliance: synthetic plan with charter passes when files in allowed_paths + status=satisfied + requires satisfied; (g) compliance fails when a file is outside allowed_paths under mode=child_commit (parametrized); (h) compliance with mode=evidence_only does NOT git-diff (just evidence checks); (i) compliance fails when status=blocked OR status=superseded (recorded in signoff but the failure's purpose is to surface, not block — actually: the signoff DOES land with the recorded status; F003's approve is what refuses re-entry); (j) compliance fails when `## Return Condition` section absent.
features.acceptance: (1) `nested_orchestration.py` adds `ChildCharter` + `CommitPolicy` Pydantic models with documented validators. `kind='governance_design'` is rejected at parse time with a deferral message pointing to v2 plan. **`commit_policy.mode` default is `evidence_only` (D003)**; `may_edit_product_code` has no default and must be explicitly set; cross-field invariant binds `mode` and `may_edit_product_code` together (both must agree on intent). (2) `plan_loader.LoadedPlan` gains `child_charter` and `commit_policy` optional fields; cross-validation rejects charter without `orchestration.parent_plan_id`. (3) **`## Return Condition` structured section (D004)**: `parse_return_condition_section` returns `Literal['satisfied','blocked','superseded']`; raises `ReturnConditionError` on missing section, missing status line, illegal value (e.g., 'partial', 'wip', 'done'), or multiple status lines. Substring matching on the close-out memo is NOT used. (4) `signoff_writer.write` gains `check_child_charter_compliance` step that runs before persistence when `child_charter` is set; raises `ChildCharterViolation` with field + observed/expected on failure; signoff envelope is NOT written on raise (no-partial-artifact, mirrors plan 005 F002 acceptance #5). (5) **Allowed-paths enforcement** (mode=child_commit only): parametrized test with synthetic plan dir + git history shows that a file modified outside `allowed_paths` triggers ChildCharterViolation; assertion message names the offending file path AND the matching glob from allowed_paths (or 'no glob matched'). Mode=evidence_only does NOT trigger this check — verified by parametrized test. (6) **Return-condition status recorded as side-car** (D008): the parsed status is persisted to `audit/charter-compliance-{plan_id}.json` (NOT inside the signoff envelope — Signoff schema in agent-conventions/v1.0 has `extra='forbid'`, so D006-style schema discipline keeps the envelope unchanged; F003 reads the side-car). `status: blocked` writes the side-car with `return_condition_status='blocked'` (does NOT raise — F003 is what refuses re-entry on non-satisfied). Missing section raises ChildCharterViolation. (7) **Requires enforcement**: parametrized test asserts each `requires` item (`patch_completeness`, `tests_pass`, `evidence_packaged`) is checked against signoff_data and raises on missing evidence. (8) **may_spawn_children defaults false**: field added to ChildCharter with `default=False`; dispatch-time grandchild-spawn refusal is wired in F003 alongside parent-pause logic. (9) **Charter-without-parent rejected**: a top-level plan (no orchestration block) with a child_charter block → plan_loader raises ValueError before dispatch. (10) `commit_policy.mode='parent_squash'` is rejected at parse time with a deferral message. (11) **Default `commit_policy` when absent** (charter present, commit_policy absent): plan_loader synthesizes `CommitPolicy(mode='evidence_only', requires=[])` — verified by test that an evidence_only-shaped charter without an explicit commit_policy block runs through compliance correctly. (12) Existing top-level plans (no charter) signoff unchanged — ZERO regression for any plan without a child_charter block.

features.description: Parent pause/fan-in protocol. New gate type `pre_resume_after_child` automatically armed on a parent plan when a child plan declaring it as parent is dispatched. Parent volley enters this gate on the next dispatch attempt while the child is in flight (detected via active-supervisor registry from F023 EC13). INBOX gains `nested_child_pending` entry shape: surfaces child plan_id, child volley status, exact `jarvis approve pre_resume_after_child --child <child_plan_id>` resume command. **events.jsonl is append-only, best-effort trace — NOT canonical state (D006).** Two new event kinds: `volley.spawn_child` (recorded when child dispatch validates pre-flight, contains parent_plan_id + child_plan_id + finding_signature + spawn_reason + timestamp) and `volley.return_to_parent` (recorded when child signoff lands, contains child_plan_id + parent_plan_id + child_final_status + return_condition_status + timestamp). The `record_event` writer swallows OSError + json.JSONEncodeError + logs a WARNING; event-write failures NEVER propagate or corrupt orchestration state. Canonical state remains plan files (plan.md, features.json), audit/gate-state.json, audit/<envelope>.json, audit/signoff-*.json — events are trace/index for human visibility, missing events are an evidence-completeness issue, never a correctness issue. Parent fan-in memo template at `evidence/fan-in-from-{child_plan_id}.md` — operator-authored, must surface what changed in the child + how the parent's `child_charter.return_condition_summary` was observed (cross-references the child's closeout-memo). **No implicit re-entry**: the parent volley does NOT auto-resume on child signoff; operator must explicitly run `jarvis approve pre_resume_after_child --child <child_plan_id>` (parity with the resume-gate-discipline contract from plan 2026-05-02-001 — bare `resume` does NOT clear this gate). **Status-satisfied gate (D004)**: the approve refuses to clear the gate unless the child's signoff records `return_condition_status: satisfied` — `blocked` or `superseded` close-outs are recorded in audit history but cannot resume the parent without an explicit operator override (a separate D-entry on the parent recording the rationale). Anti-recursion enforcement: the explicit-approval-with-status-satisfied requirement is the operator's last-mile check that the child actually resolved the parent finding before parent work resumes.
steps: Add `pre_resume_after_child` gate type to `gate_pause.py`'s known gate enum + auto-arming logic: when supervisor.dispatch_volley starts on a parent plan AND active_supervisors registry shows a child plan referencing it as parent_plan_id, auto-arm the gate via gate_pause.pause(plan_dir, [`pre_resume_after_child:{child_plan_id}`]). The plural-children case (rejected by F002 v1) doesn't arise.

Extend `inbox.py`: add `nested_child_pending` entry template that renders parent_plan_id, child_plan_id, child volley status (from active_supervisors), and the exact `jarvis approve pre_resume_after_child --child <child_id>` command. Hook into supervisor.dispatch_volley: when the parent gate auto-arms, write the INBOX entry once (idempotent — re-dispatches don't append duplicates).

Add `events.jsonl` writer surface to `nested_orchestration.py` (or new `events_log.py` module): `record_event(plan_dir, kind, payload)` appends one JSON object per line. **Best-effort discipline (D006)**: wrap append in try/except (OSError, TypeError, json.JSONEncodeError); on failure, log WARNING with kind + plan_id + reason and return silently. Never raise. Two new event kinds: `volley.spawn_child` (recorded by supervisor.dispatch_volley on a child plan after orchestration validation passes; fields: parent_plan_id, child_plan_id, spawn_reason, finding_signature, ts) and `volley.return_to_parent` (recorded by signoff_writer on the child plan when signoff lands; fields: child_plan_id, parent_plan_id, child_final_status, return_condition_status, ts). The parent's events.jsonl receives the spawn_child entry; the child's events.jsonl receives the return_to_parent entry — symmetric, both files reflect the relationship.

Add `evidence/fan-in-from-{child_plan_id}.md` template generator: when operator runs `jarvis approve pre_resume_after_child --child <id>` on the parent plan, the CLI checks for a fan-in memo at the expected path; if missing, refuses to clear the gate with a message naming the expected path + a stub-template suggestion. Operator authors the memo (text-only, no machine validation in v1) and re-runs the approve. The memo's existence is the explicit signal that operator has reviewed the child's outcome.

CLI: extend `jarvis approve` to accept `pre_resume_after_child --child <child_plan_id>` shape. Validation: child_plan_id must match a real plan dir, child must have signoff with final_status set AND `return_condition_status: satisfied`, fan-in memo must exist at expected path. Status ∈ {`blocked`, `superseded`} → refused unless `--accept-non-satisfied` is passed (operator override; CLI prompts to record rationale in plan's decisions.jsonl but does not enforce). Bare `resume <plan>` does NOT clear `pre_resume_after_child:*` gates (parity with resume-gate-discipline D004 from plan 2026-05-02-001 — plan-level bulk-clear discipline).

Tests: `test_parent_pause_protocol.py` covers (a) gate auto-arms when child dispatch is detected via active_supervisors; (b) INBOX entry rendered correctly with idempotence (multiple parent re-dispatches don't append duplicate entries); (c) events.jsonl spawn_child + return_to_parent entries appear in correct files (parent receives spawn, child receives return); (d) **best-effort events**: when events.jsonl path is read-only, `record_event` returns silently and orchestration state lands correctly; (e) fan-in memo absence blocks approve (CLI exits non-zero with expected-path message); (f) fan-in memo present + child signoff with `return_condition_status=satisfied` + correct child_plan_id → approve clears the gate; (g) **status-satisfied gate**: child with status=blocked → approve refuses; child with status=superseded → approve refuses; `--accept-non-satisfied` flag with status=blocked → approve clears (operator override path); (h) bare `resume <plan>` does NOT clear pre_resume_after_child gate (asserts gate-state.json unchanged); (i) **canonical state primacy**: events.jsonl deleted on both parent and child mid-flow → approve still works because gate-state + signoff carry the load-bearing info; (j) hermetic synthetic e2e: full sequence (spawn parent → spawn child → child signoff satisfied → parent gate → memo → approve → resume) under tmp_path with scripted executors.
features.acceptance: (1) New gate type `pre_resume_after_child` added to `gate_pause.py`; auto-arms on parent volley dispatch when active_supervisors shows a referencing child. Gate name format: `pre_resume_after_child:{child_plan_id}` to permit multiple children in v2 (v1 will only ever have one entry). (2) INBOX `nested_child_pending` entry shape renders parent_plan_id + child_plan_id + child status + the exact approve command; idempotent (re-dispatch doesn't duplicate). (3) **`events.jsonl` is best-effort trace, not canonical state (D006)**: ships with `record_event(plan_dir, kind, payload)` that opens the file in append mode, writes one JSON object per line, and on OSError or json.JSONEncodeError logs a WARNING and returns silently — never propagates. Two new event kinds (`volley.spawn_child`, `volley.return_to_parent`). The parent's events.jsonl gets the spawn_child entry; the child's gets the return_to_parent entry. Test verifies (a) successful append produces well-formed JSONL; (b) when the events.jsonl path is read-only or the dir is unwritable, `record_event` does NOT raise and orchestration state (gate-state, audit envelopes, signoff) lands correctly anyway. (4) **No implicit re-entry**: parent volley does NOT auto-resume on child signoff. Test asserts that after child signoff lands, running `dispatch_volley` on the parent re-enters the `pre_resume_after_child` gate (still armed) until explicit approve clears it. (5) Fan-in memo enforcement: `jarvis approve pre_resume_after_child --child <id>` refuses to clear the gate when `evidence/fan-in-from-{child_plan_id}.md` is missing on the parent plan; the error message names the expected path. (6) **Status-satisfied gate (D004)**: the approve refuses to clear the gate unless the child's signoff records `return_condition_status: satisfied`. When the child's signoff has `return_condition_status` ∈ {`blocked`, `superseded`}, approve refuses and the error message surfaces the recorded status + the close-out memo path. The operator can override via `--accept-non-satisfied` flag, which is recorded as a free-form D-entry requirement on the parent (CLI prompts the operator to record the rationale, but does NOT enforce a D-file write — that remains operator hygiene). (7) **Bare-resume discipline (parity with plan 2026-05-02-001 D004)**: bare `jarvis resume <parent_plan_id>` does NOT clear `pre_resume_after_child:*` gates; only the explicit `--child <id>` flag clears them. Verified by parametrized test asserting gate-state.json's cleared_gates does NOT include the pre_resume_after_child entry after a bare resume. (8) Fan-in memo template stub: when operator runs approve and memo is missing, the CLI's error message includes a 6-line stub template (sections: 'What changed in the child', 'How the parent return_condition_summary was observed', 'Open follow-ups') that operator can paste in. (9) **Symmetric events**: parent and child both have events.jsonl files with the relationship recorded — operator can read either side and reconstruct the chain. The reconstructed chain MUST be derivable from the canonical state alone (plan files + gate-state + audit + signoff) — events are merely an index — so a test verifies that with events.jsonl artificially deleted from both sides, the canonical state still permits identifying the parent/child relationship. (10) **Hermetic synthetic e2e test (D005)**: the canonical acceptance proof. Synthetic test exercises the full sequence under a tmp_path: spawn parent → spawn child referencing parent → child runs to signoff with status=satisfied → parent dispatch enters gate → operator authors fan-in memo → operator approves → parent resumes. Same test parametrized for status=blocked → approve refuses; status=superseded → approve refuses. Real-dogfood trial is OPTIONAL evidence (recorded if a clean recursive-finding case surfaces during impl), NOT a hard acceptance criterion (D005). (11) Existing plans (no nested orchestration) are unaffected — gate auto-arming is conditional on `LoadedPlan.orchestration is not None` for the child + active_supervisors registry showing it as in-flight. (12) **Canonical state primacy (D006)**: a parametrized test deletes `events.jsonl` mid-flow on both parent and child, then verifies that the parent can still complete approve correctly because canonical state (gate-state, signoff with return_condition_status) carries the load-bearing information.
